Mrs. Florence R. Hopkins may be appointed for one year, upon request of the Secretary of the Treasury, without compliance with the civil service rules, to a suitable position in the Treasury Department, but shall not by such appointment and service acquire a classified status or right to further employment. Mrs. Hopkins is the widow of Henry I. Hopkins, who spent eighteen years in the Government service, and died on June 14, 1926, from injuries the cause of which has never been determined. Mrs. Hopkins has four dependent children to support and is without adequate means of support. HERBERT HOOVER The White House, May 12, 1930. Mrs. Hopkins was appointed a copyist in the War Department on June 15, 1893, and served until 1905.

August 19, 1915. First Sergeant William Feldman, United States Army, retired, may be admitted to examination for the classified service. Paragraph 1, civil-service Rule V, which provides that no person shall be admitted to examination unless he be a citizen of or owe allegiance to the United States, is hereby waived in his favor. Mr. Feldman is technically not a citizen of the United States, notwithstanding his service in the Army. In view of his honorable Army service of over 25 years, he being retired as first sergeant of Troop F, Sixth Cavalry, the commission concurs with the Secretary of War in recommending that Mr. Feldman be admitted to examination under waiver of the rule and with the understanding that he will without delay take the necessary steps to acquire citizenship.

June 28, 1916. Miss Rachael C. McKeown, of Maryland, may be appointed to a position as clerk at $900 per annum in the Bureau of Animal Industry in the Department of Agriculture without reference to the civil-service rules. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Agriculture, who states that Miss McKeown is the daughter of Dr. Thomas H. McKeown, formerly a veterinary inspector in the Bureau of Animal Industry, who died on April 12, 1916, as the result of an automobile accident which occurred while he was in the discharge of his official duties. Throughout his connection with the department his services were satisfactory.

Taft Monday, January 30, 1911 1910 CSR 116 650405Executive Order 1293 — Authorizing Reinstatement of Archibald Edmonstone as Assistant Weigher in Customs Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules1911President of the United States Mr. Archibald Edmonstone was removed from the position of weigher in the Customs Service at New York on May 11, 1909, with three other weighers, who were believed to be responsible for much of the corruption in their division. It appears from the statements of the collector, of the Chief of the Appointment Division of the Treasury Department, and of Mr. Henry L. Stimson, who investigated the frauds, that the evidence not only failed to connect Mr. Edmonstone with the frauds but that the testimony of all of the witnesses who were examined was unanimous in stating that he never participated in the frauds. It appears that Mr. Edmonstone was an efficient and upright employee. In view of the facts it is ordered that Mr. Edmonstone may be reinstated to the position of assistant weigher in compliance with the request of the Secretary of the Treasury which is concurred in by the Civil Service Commission. Dr. Park Howell may be appointed as acting assistant surgeon in the Public Health Service, for a period not to exceed one year, without compliance with the civil-service rules and regulations. October 22, 1913. Mrs. Mary R. Geddings may be appointed to a position in the classified service with out reference to the requirement of examination under the civil-service rules. Mrs. Geddings is the widow of Surg. Henry D. Geddings, of the Public Health Serv- ice, who was a commissioned medical officer in that service for about 25 years, and who rendered distinguished service in matters relating to sanitation and public health. He also rendered valuable service in several epidemics of yellow fever at a time when few medical men were immune to that disease and its cause was but little known. The Secretary of the Treasury states that it would be a fitting testimonial to the serv- ices of Surg. January 19, 191%. Mr. Austin F. Hawes may be reinstated as extension specialist in forestry at a salary of $2,760 per annum in the States Relations Service of the Department of Agriculture without regard to the year limit of the reinstatement rule. Mr. Hawes was appointed a forest assistant in 1903 through examination under the civil-service rules, and served until 1906, when he became State forester of Con- necticut. In 1909 he became State forester of Vermont and professor of forestry at the University of Vermont. The Department of Agriculture states that it is believed that his reinstatement would be in the interests of good administration. The Civil Service Commission concurs in recommending this order.

May 7, 1913. Mr. John E. Hollingsworth, of Texas, who entered the classified service by virtue of a competitive examination as post office inspector, may be reinstated without regard to the year limitation as ie by the civil service rules. This order is issued on the recommendation of the Postmaster General, in view of the fact that his separation from the service was without any fault, delinquency, or mis- conduct on his part whatsoever.

April 28, 1916. Miss Ella Lee, of Mississippi, may be appointed to a clerical position in the Postal Service, with a view to her appointment in the post office at Jackson, Miss., without reference to the requirements of the civil-service rules. Miss Lee is the daughter of the late Robert C. Lee, who for many years was United States district attorney for the southern district of Mississippi, and whose death about a year ago, together with the recent death of her brother, renders it necessary for Miss Lee to secure employment in order to provide a livelihood for herself and mother. It is stated that Miss Lee is a graduate of the high school of Jackson and well qualified to fill a clerical position in the Postal Serv- ice, and that the postmaster will appoint her to such a position if authorized to do so.
